actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The Engine default configuration uses the car model: 'robot_base': 'xmls/car.xml'
Engine builds a Robot from the configured robot XML before it derives the action space
The action space is Box(-1, 1, (robot.nu,)): one control between -1 and 1 per actuator of the robot model
Robot loads the configured XML with load_model_from_path and takes nu (the actuator count) from the loaded model
car.xml sets the simulation timestep to 0.004 s
The car model default motor has ctrlrange -1 1, ctrllimited true, forcerange -0.02 0.02 and forcelimited true
car.xml declares a free joint named robot, two hinge joints named left and right, and a ball joint named rear
car.xml has two motors, both jointinparent transmissions with gear 1, so the model has two actuators
The xmls README states each robot XML should be complete and simulate-able as-is
The xmls README states each robot XML should include actuators which provide control
The xmls README says a robot scene should be clear of other objects, with only the robot in the scene
The Engine default ends an episode after 1000 environment steps
One Engine step advances the simulation by a binomial draw of up to 10 physics steps, and the default probability 1.0 makes it 10 steps
Engine.step clips the action to the model's actuator_ctrlrange before writing data.ctrl

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults (mj_resetData), so a run repeats on one engine but no seed selects a different state

gaps: the driver steps the robot model of car.xml alone: the Engine's task objects, goal, hazards, vases, lidar and cost/reward are not modelled (xmls/README.md:14-16) and cap.world.step.v1 carries no reward

the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the joint layout and the actuator control ranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint, so trajectories, contacts, friction, free-joint dynamics and sensors are not MuJoCo's

the Engine advances an environment step by a binomial draw of up to 10 physics steps at p=1.0 (engine.py:287-291) and ends an episode after 1000 environment steps (engine.py:98); this driver's ticks are physics steps of the model, and it declares no episode and no truncation

the Engine clips an action to actuator_ctrlrange (engine.py:1245-1247); this driver instead refuses a ctrl outside the model's actuator_ctrlrange before any call, because the runtime rejects rather than clamps

the car model uses MuJoCo 2.0-era mujoco_py syntax (jointinparent transmissions at car.xml:54-55 and <size njmax="3000" nconmax="1000"> at car.xml:2); the modern mujoco library was not installed where the gate ran, so whether it loads this file was not verified
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no rendering is offered and no physical car robot is modelled; nothing was validated against a device

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
